title: Python attribute-write: the F1c bare-name from-import base and the from m import m2 non-module-file residual are known dev-equal gaps (#245 N3)
description: Filed from the opum-ai/glyph-cli#245 round-1 reviewer item N3, which asked that F1c stop being described as a control and become a known dev-equal gap with its own follow-up. TWO RESIDUALS, both dev-equal today, so nothing is red-before: (1) the BARE-NAME variant of the written base — from m import B; class K(B) — answers external on dev d58878f, on 034a898 and on the GCLI-161 head, with and without a write m.B = L, because the write does not reach the bare-name read on dev. (2) from m import m2 where m2 is not a module file: the from-import carries a non-module name and the reader answers it as dev does, not as a written module attribute would. GCLI-156 relabels the F1c fixture as a known gap (N3) and pins the current behaviour; this task is the follow-up that decides whether either residual is a defect against the rules or a documented limitation. Bring a bounded A/B to opum-doc if the build does not fit two rounds. Fixture lives in test/python-hops.test.ts F1c. No DEC-182 path class, no dependency.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each residual is measured on the current dev and the GCLI-161 landing before any build, and the measurement is recorded with the shape it names

The decision for each residual — defect with a red-before/green-after fixture and a mutant, or documented limitation with the measurement that justifies it — is recorded and linked from the F1c fixture comment
No DEC-182 path class is touched and no dependency is added
